chapters.note: The census order, names and quantities remain. “Head by head” and the distinction between the army and the Levites are retained. Ordinary address now uses you/your.
The camp order, directions, named leaders and totals remain. The inherited southwest and seaward language has not been replaced with a different geographical system.

The Levite divisions and firstborn redemption remain. Numerical discrepancies, including 3:34 and the total in 3:39, have not been silently harmonized. Specialist review of these figures remains pending.
The age limits, objects, coverings, ritual agents and totals remain. The negative purpose clause in 4:15 and the prohibition in 4:18 have clearer English grammar.

The distinctions among uncleanness, restitution, accusation and testing remain. Conditional clauses use ordinary present-tense English. The bodily language is retained without substituting a modern medical interpretation.

The inherited consecration terminology and the parenthesis following 6:23 remain. In 6:24–26 the blessing addresses its human recipients, so “you” replaces “thee”; the Lord is spoken of in the third person.
All twelve repeated offerings, their quantities and their order remain. List punctuation now connects the successive verse units; repetition has not been compressed.
The distinct actions of Moses, Aaron, the Levites and the people remain. The inherited wording of 8:19 and 8:26 is retained for specialist review; ordinary address uses you/your.
The appointed Passover times, exception and repeated movements of the cloud remain. Conditional clauses and the sentence about one law for native and sojourner have clearer English grammar.
The trumpet signals and camp sequence remain. Direct address to God in 10:34 retains Thine/Thee. The existing source order of 10:34–36 is unchanged.

Moses’ direct address to God retains Thou/Thee/Thy and the corresponding verb forms. Within 11:12, God’s quoted command to Moses uses “your”. The images of carrying the people, manna, wind and quail remain.

Punctuation in 12:4 now correctly places Moses, Miriam and Aaron among the recipients before the command begins, following a selected main-text check. The stray comma in 12:10 is removed. The prayer in 12:13 retains Thee.
The names, route, fruit, report and opposing responses remain. The questions about the land in 13:18–20 have clearer English syntax; inherited source-specific names are not harmonized.

The doubled “exceedingly” in 14:7 remains. Moses’ direct address to God retains Thou/Thy; ordinary address uses you/your. The children, Caleb, forty years and repeated warnings retain their distinct places in the account.

The offerings, measures, shared law and distinction between unintentional and presumptuous acts remain. The English conditional in 15:14 is clarified within the inherited interpretation; its Greek clause relationship remains a priority for independent syntactic review.
The separate speakers, challenges, offerings and judgments remain. Conditional verbs in 16:29–30 use ordinary present-tense English. The inherited wording of 16:14 and 16:22 remains provisional.

All 28 source-numbered units remain in their existing order, including the fire pans, outbreak and staffs. The contrast between the dead and living and the repeated report that the outbreak subsided remain.
The distinctions among priestly and Levite duties, portions, redemption and tithes remain. Attributive “thine” becomes “your”; possessive “thine” becomes “yours”. The covenant of salt remains.
The ritual agents, ashes, living water, contact rules and third/seventh-day sequence remain. The inherited statement in 19:19 is retained without silently reconciling it with another reading.
The instructions, the two strikes, the responses and Aaron’s death remain. Ordinary speech between Israel and Edom uses you/your; source-specific wording such as Aaron’s being “released” remains.

The direct vow to God in 21:2 retains Thou. The mixed complaint against God and Moses in 21:5 retains the draft’s ordinary-address treatment; its singular addressee remains a question for review. The bronze-serpent instructions, songs and place names remain.

Ordinary address, including speech to the donkey and the angel, uses you/your. The account’s changes between past narration and historical present are retained. “Means of divination” remains provisional.
The repeated altars, sacrifices and blessings remain. The inherited oracle wording, including “one-horned beast”, is retained; specialist identification and syntax review remain pending.

The inherited Gog, man/star language, Beor and Og readings remain after selected main-text inspection. The difficult opening of 24:17 is retained provisionally; the negative clause has clearer English word order. No new manuscript choice is claimed.
The agents, reported actions, names, plague total and covenant language remain. Difficult inherited wording in 25:4, 25:6 and 25:8 is retained for specialist review.
The source order of the tribes, every name and every stated quantity remain. Numerical or genealogical difficulties, including 26:59, have not been silently repaired.

The inheritance sequence and appointment of Joshua remain. Conditional verbs use ordinary present-tense English; the negative in 27:14 has clearer word order. “Judgment of the manifestations” remains provisional.
The daily, Sabbath, new-moon and festival offerings retain their order and quantities. Sentence order and punctuation clarify the instructions without reducing repeated sacrificial language.
All eight days, changing cattle totals, repeated offerings and stated additions remain. Ordinary address uses you/your; the recurring formulas are not compressed.
All 17 source-numbered units remain. Conditional clauses now use ordinary present-tense English; the distinctions among vows, restrictions, silence, refusal and annulment remain.

The reported violence, captives, purification instructions, quantities, division of spoils and memorial offering remain without euphemistic substitution. “Does not pass through fire” clarifies the English negative.

Punctuation in 32:2 now places Moses, Eleazar and the rulers among the recipients before the list of towns begins, following a selected main-text check. The conditions for crossing and receiving the allotment have clearer English grammar.
All stations, repeated departures and encampments, dates and names remain. The additional itinerary statement in 33:36 and the inherited commands in 33:52–56 are retained.
The inherited boundaries, directions and names remain. The repeated “mountain, the mountain” in 34:7–8 is retained as a source question, rather than replaced by an assumed modern identification.

The distinctions among unintentional killing, murder, refuge, witnesses and ransom remain. Conditional verbs now use ordinary present-tense English. The inherited distances and high-priest provisions remain.
The inheritance question, restriction and daughters’ response remain. “Release” is retained; the opening conditional in 36:4 now uses “comes”.

scope: English editorial review; selected main-text checks. Full independent Greek, apparatus, reception and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
